AC-1.class: Alter the recorded action — arguments, result, approval decision

AC-2.class: Alter an event and repair the citing digest

AC-3.class: Re-sign rewritten history with the current key
AC-3.note: Carried from M2 to M3a. The ratchet makes yesterday's record unforgeable with today's key, but an operator holding the current key can still re-sign a rewritten history within the current epoch — and nothing local can refuse that. The countersignature over the original root is the half that contradicts it, so the class closes only when both exist. The red-team suite names both for attack C2 and always did; M2 claiming the gate alone would have been the plan disagreeing with the suite.

AC-5.class: Erase events and renumber into a clean stream

AC-6.class: Stop or patch the collector, then claim quiet

AC-7.class: Weaken the anchoring policy, then tamper

milestones.name: Foundations and long-lead
milestones.goal: Start everything whose clock runs outside engineering, and turn the red-team suite into the acceptance harness.
milestones.exit: Trademark search returned and recorded. Counsel engagement deferred to a funded release. Threat model published. CI runs the canary, the DCO check and all three validators. Harness inverted so each attack class can assert DETECTED against our own verifier. Bounty adjudication removed rather than outsourced, so no arbiter is required.

milestones.name: Local integrity
milestones.goal: Close the two attack classes that need no third party, and measure the performance budget before the design hardens.
milestones.exit: Red-team A and C both DETECTED by splitstick verify; baseline still passes. p99 append overhead measured under 1 ms and run latency under 2% — measured, not assumed. Chain files contain no plaintext. First package published with a provenance attestation and an SBOM, so the build digest M4 relies on can be traced to its source.

milestones.name: Key custody
milestones.goal: Make yesterday's record unforgeable with today's key, and state the precondition honestly.
milestones.exit: An epoch-N key cannot produce a valid epoch-N-1 signature. The succession chain walks from a pinned root and a skipped or self-endorsing epoch is refused. The non-exportable custody precondition appears wherever the forward-secrecy claim does, and the verifier refuses the claim outright for any epoch declared software-keyed. M2 closes no attack class on its own: AC-3 needs the countersignature and is carried to M3a.

milestones.name: Anchoring and sequencing
milestones.goal: The first second party. Close truncation and erasure, which no amount of local cryptography can reach.
milestones.exit: Red-team C2, D, E and F all DETECTED. A run with no configuration at all anchors to a public log the project does not operate. A rolled-back witness is detected. An auditor supplying their own acceptance policy verifies the same pack. Egress captured against real witness traffic, confirming no content leaves the host. AC-3 closes here rather than in M2, because a re-signed history is contradicted by a countersignature over the original root and by nothing local.

carries.why: Carried into M3a from M2 and NOT closed here. The KMS half is built and covered (packages/signer-aws-kms) and needs only the operator's key to run. The HSM half is blocked by evidence rather than effort and nothing in M3a changed that: of the products that sign Ed25519, AWS KMS issues no per-key attestation and GCP offers the algorithm at software protection level only, so independently-supported custody still requires hardware, and the YubiHSM 2 purchase is held. FR-70's validator now exists and is correct, but it has only ever been run against documents this project constructed — every result carries provider_untested: true to say so. See docs/kms-capability-matrix.md and docs/m3a-failure-modes.md.
carries.closes: A hardware signer behind the same sign(bytes) seam, with an integration test proving its signature verifies under an independent Ed25519 implementation, and FR-70's five checks exercised against a REAL provider attestation rather than a constructed one. M7 is the right home because the launch gate is where every published claim has to have evidence behind it, and 'operate with a KMS or HSM' is a published claim.

milestones.gate_evidence_note: AC-3, AC-4 and AC-5 cannot be closed by anything local, which is the project's thesis rather than a shortfall. They are claimed in the configuration M3a delivers: a stateful witness (FR-17) countersigning checkpoints, and its retained heights in the reader's hands (FR-54). The SHIPPED DEFAULT (FR-48: TSA + OpenTimestamps) does NOT provide this — a TSA signs your hash and forgets you — so an operator who leaves the default in place has not closed 4 and 5, and DES-08 says so. The gate records that the mechanism works when configured, not that every deployment has it.

milestones.name: Practice statement and resilience
milestones.goal: Say exactly what the countersignature means, and make sure losing a witness does not lose the evidence.
milestones.exit: Practice statement published, versioned and itself anchored, naming its time discipline. An agent run completes normally with every witness unreachable. Restore drill meets the stated recovery point objective. Countersignatures from a retired witness key still verify. Operator key compromise recoverable as a declared, countersigned discontinuity.

milestones.name: Coverage attestation
milestones.goal: The differentiated claim: prove the record is complete, not merely unaltered.
milestones.exit: Killing the collector produces a detectable gap. Patching it reports an unrecognised build digest. Downgrading the witness policy appears as a countersigned chain event. A declared gap lets the sequence recover without a silent reset.

milestones.name: Disclosure and erasure
milestones.goal: No new attack class. This is the milestone that makes the product buyable by a regulated, multi-customer organisation.
milestones.exit: Verification passes after content and key deletion. A single-event disclosure verifies in isolation against a countersigned root. A 100,000-event run verifies in under 2 seconds with no network and no credentials. Both metadata leaks documented.

milestones.name: Reach and conformance
milestones.goal: Stop depending on one upstream project, and make the format genuinely somebody else's to implement.
milestones.exit: End-to-end capture against two non-OMA runtimes over both MCP transports. A third-party witness passes the published conformance suite. A fully self-hosted deployment verified at zero egress, with no account and no enrolment with us. The conformance suite fuzzes the canonicaliser rather than only driving fixed vectors, because a fixed-vector suite is exactly what missed the surrogate collision in M1.

carries.why: M1 proved canonicalisation completeness with a property test that mutates every field at every depth, and an independent review still found a collision it could not reach: two records differing only by an unpaired surrogate produced identical canonical bytes and identical leaves. The test only mutates values that round-trip through JSON, so no amount of running it would ever have found that.
carries.closes: FR-46's conformance suite fuzzes the canonicaliser rather than only driving fixed vectors: unpaired surrogates, numbers at the representable boundary, deeply nested structures, keys that collide after Unicode normalisation. The property asserted is that distinct inputs never share canonical bytes.

milestones.name: Launch gate
milestones.goal: Every promise that is a claim rather than a feature. This milestone is mostly about what we must not say.
milestones.exit: Claims audit clean across all sixteen scope guards. Every published figure has a passing benchmark behind it. Bounty terms published, stating plainly that recognition is non-cash while the project is unfunded. No surface anywhere claims conformity, certification, or tamper-proofing. NFR-01 has a qualifying acceptance measurement on the reference environment and NFR-02 has been re-measured against a real provider; neither may be reported as met on a development-machine number.

carries.why: M1 measured the append path and revised the budget to p95 under 1 ms and p99 under 3 ms, but no run has qualified: the development machine reports itself a regression metric on load average, event count and repeats. The numbers recorded against it are measurements, not acceptance.
carries.closes: One run of bench/append.mjs over at least 1e6 events and at least three repeats, on a machine meeting every constraint in bench/reference-env.json, with --machine and --storage named. The harness prints QUALIFYING ACCEPTANCE MEASUREMENT only when nothing is short; that JSON becomes the requirement evidence.

carries.why: The 2 percent budget is established against a scripted model and an assumed 400 ms per model call. Both assumptions are recorded in the result, and neither has been tested against a real provider.
carries.closes: Re-measure the interleaved paired A/B against a real provider once one is in the loop, and confirm the 95 percent interval still clears the budget at that model latency.

carries.why: Re-carried from M3a. The KMS half is delivered and awaits a key; the HSM half is blocked on hardware whose attestation capability is unconfirmed. Deciding it at the launch gate is the honest place: that is where a published claim must have evidence.
carries.closes: Either a real HSM attestation through FR-70's five checks, or the claim narrowed in the published text to what the KMS half actually supports. One of those two, explicitly, and not a third option where the claim stands unevidenced.

regressionRule: Every milestone runs the complete red-team suite, not only its own classes. A gate closed earlier that reopens fails the build.
